complications.title: Ketoacidosis: liver and metabolism

views.label: Liver
views.text: Without insulin the liver releases glucose and turns fatty acids into ketones. It is enlarged and fatty.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: Pale, greasy, swollen liver. Fat from the adipose tissue is stored in hepatocytes.

views.label: Hepatocytes
views.text: Fat vacuoles accumulate and mitochondria make ketone bodies. Flow through the sinusoid is normal.

*.body: The liver is the ketone factory. With no insulin and high glucagon it makes glucose and turns fat into ketones.
*.care: Insulin switches ketone production off. Fluids and potassium come first.

**.body: Fat mobilised from adipose tissue is oxidised to ketones in the mitochondria, then released into the blood.
**.care: Insulin infusion with potassium replacement closes the gap.

complications.reversibleText: Fully reversible once insulin, fluids and electrolytes are given. The fatty change resolves over days.

complications.title: Osmotic diuresis and volume loss

views.label: Kidney
views.text: Glucose in the urine drags water, sodium and potassium out. The kidney is under-perfused and can be injured.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: Pale cortex with a congested medulla. The injury is pre-renal if volume is restored early.

views.label: Tubule
views.text: Saturated glucose transporters leave glucose in the lumen, which holds water there.

*.body: Above about 180 mg per dL the tubule cannot reclaim all the filtered glucose. Water and electrolytes follow it out.
*.care: Replace the fluid deficit first, then add insulin. Avoid a rapid fall in osmolality.

**.body: Glucose that the transporters cannot reabsorb stays in the lumen and holds water there. Potassium is lost with it.

complications.reversibleText: Reversible with fluid replacement. Delay and shock can turn pre-renal injury into tubular necrosis.

complications.title: Cerebral oedema in DKA

views.label: Brain
views.text: Flattened gyri and tight sulci. Brain cells swell, mostly in children, when osmolality falls too fast.

views.label: Cut surface
views.text: Soft, wet brain with a blurred grey-white boundary and compressed ventricles.

views.label: Neurone and barrier
views.text: Brain cells hold on to solute, then take in water as plasma osmolality falls. The barrier leaks.

*.body: The brain swells inside a rigid skull. Rapid correction of glucose and osmolality draws water into brain cells.
*.care: Mannitol or hypertonic saline if oedema is suspected. Slow the fall in osmolality.

**.body: Cells that adapted to high osmolality take up water when the blood becomes dilute too quickly.
**.care: Avoid fluid boluses beyond what is needed and a rapid fall in glucose.

complications.reversibleText: Often reversible if recognised early and treated at once. Herniation is fatal or severely disabling.
